newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK manufacturing, industrial data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK manufacturing, industrial data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to data showing November UK manufacturing output down 0.5 percent m/m and up 0.2 percent y/y and industrial production up 0.4 percent m/m and 1.3 percent y/y:
"Very surprising. It may well be that the appreciation in sterling is having an impact on manufacturing output much earlier than most of us had been expecting."

"We have to recognise that manufacturing numbers are very erratic. I think it is far too early to attribute this drop in manufacturing output to sterling's appreciation. Frankly I think it just reflects the erratic nature of the numbers and I would expect either this number to be revised or a decent rebound in December. You have to look at the underlying trend and at the survey numbers. Whilst the survey numbers ahead are showing some weakness in export orders, they are still showing manufacturing output rising, so I'd be very surprised if this was the start of a new decline in manufacturing production activity."
MARIAN BELL, ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND

"With industry worried by sterling strength, surprisingly soft UK November manufacturing output will be taken negatively by sterling. Survey evidence suggests a bigger sterling effect in December. As with the fall in the key year on year balance in the CBI December retail report overnight, the data are gilt and short sterling positive."
